findings.title: Sign-in code requests carry no CAPTCHA: anyone can make Supabase Auth mail codes to the owner's address and spend the Resend daily quota that receipts need
findings.evidence: SignIn.tsx:36-39 calls `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, options: { shouldCreateUser: false } })` with no `captchaToken`; supabase/config.toml:218-222 leaves `[auth.captcha]` commented out, and ISSUES.md I28 (the hosted Auth settings list) names no CAPTCHA and no `email_sent` value. supabase/functions/_shared/outbox.ts:36-55: `DAILY_QUOTA = 100` (Resend free, 'daily email quota of 100 emails/day'), and 'Sign-in codes do not travel through the outbox — Supabase Auth sends them over its own SMTP connection'. Vendor: Supabase rate limits (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/rate-limits): /auth/v1/otp is limited per user to one request per 60 s and per IP to 30 per 5 min; the project-wide 'emails sent' limit is 'customizable when you use custom SMTP'. Supabase Auth source (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/auth/master/internal/api/api.go): `/otp` is wrapped in `api.verifyCaptcha`, so a CAPTCHA would gate it once enabled.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated attacker who knows a staff address (Anas's is public) POSTs /auth/v1/otp from rotating IPs once a minute: up to 60 Arabic sign-in codes an hour land in the owner's inbox, and every one is a Resend send on the same account as receipts. Resend's free 100/day is reached in under two hours; the outbox then reads 429 as QUOTA and holds receipts, order-access links and owner alerts until the next 00:00 UTC (DATA-AND-SECURITY 'Email delivery'). Paying buyers get no receipt or order link for up to a day, and staff cannot sign in because their codes are refused too. Precondition: the hosted project's 'emails sent' rate limit is left at a value above ~4/hour (I28 sets none). With Resend's 3,000/month free quota the same loop empties the whole month in two to four days, and while the quota is spent Supabase Auth itself cannot deliver codes, so staff are locked out of the admin too (the sign-in form even reports the failed send as sent, CLIENT-SEC-10). The project's own evidence file PLANS/evidence/runtime-supabase-production.txt:123 quotes Supabase's advice to put CAPTCHA on sign-in and password-reset endpoints; no plan item took it up.
findings.proposed_fix: Enable Auth CAPTCHA (Turnstile, which the site already uses) on the hosted project and in `[auth.captcha]` for local, render the Turnstile widget on the sign-in email step and pass `options.captchaToken` to `signInWithOtp`; record in I28 an 'emails sent' limit sized for the staff (for example 10 per hour) so the Auth path alone can never spend the Resend day. Add both to the P11 hosted checklist.
findings.proof_recipe: Against a stack with custom SMTP configured: `for i in 1..5: curl -X POST $SUPABASE_URL/auth/v1/otp -H 'apikey: <publishable>' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"<owner>","create_user":false}'` spaced 61 s apart (or from different IPs). Expected wrong result: every call answers 200 and a mail is sent each time (no captcha_required error); after enabling CAPTCHA the same call answers 400 `captcha verification process failed`.

findings.title: The Auth API tells an unknown address from a staff address (422 otp_disabled vs 200), so the UI's masked «إن كان هذا البريد مسجّلًا» hides nothing from an attacker
findings.evidence: SignIn.tsx:17-20 comment: 'Step 1 never reveals whether the address is a staff email; only a rate limit varies the message', and lines 43-52 map every non-429 answer to SENT_MESSAGE. The request is `signInWithOtp({ email, options: { shouldCreateUser: false } })`. Supabase Auth source (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/auth/master/internal/api/otp.go): with `create_user: false` and no such user, `shouldCreateUser` returns false and the handler answers 422 with code `otp_disabled`, message 'Signups not allowed for otp'; a known address answers 200 and sends the code. tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts:9-14 ("an unknown email gets the identical sent message") asserts only the UI sentence, so the suite proves nothing about the API oracle.
findings.impact: Anyone with the publishable key (it is in every page) can enumerate which addresses are staff accounts by calling /auth/v1/otp directly, one probe per address, under the 30-per-5-minutes-per-IP limit. Combined with CLIENT-SEC-01 it tells the attacker which inboxes to flood; on its own it confirms staff membership of a guessed address.
findings.proposed_fix: Correct the comment and the P03 claim (the masking is UI-only; Supabase's OTP endpoint is the oracle). The CAPTCHA of CLIENT-SEC-01 bounds the probing rate; no client code can remove the oracle, so the plan should state it as a known residual rather than a property.
findings.proof_recipe: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST $SUPABASE_URL/auth/v1/otp -H 'apikey: <publishable>' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"nobody-xyz@example.com","create_user":false}' → expect 422; repeat with a real staff address → expect 200.

findings.title: Password-recovery mail is still a sign-in-by-link path for staff: the hook lets `recovery` through and the hosted template is the English default with a link
findings.evidence: deny_password_tokens refuses only `authentication_method = 'password'` (line 27) and its own comment (line 18) lists 'recovery' among the methods passed 'through unchanged'. supabase/config.toml:254-262 customises only `magic_link` (code only, `{{ .Token }}`); no `[auth.email.template.recovery]` exists, and I28's hosted list names only the magic-link template. Supabase Auth's `/auth/v1/recover` is unauthenticated and sends the default 'Reset Password' mail whose `{{ .ConfirmationURL }}` is a `/auth/v1/verify?type=recovery` link that creates a session and redirects to the site with the tokens in the fragment. The hook docs list `recovery` as an authentication_method (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook).
findings.impact: Anyone can make Supabase send Anas (or any staff address) an English 'Reset your password' mail from the studio's sender, one per 60 s per address, without CAPTCHA (same channel as CLIENT-SEC-01). The link in it is a one-time sign-in: a mail-scanner prefetch burns it harmlessly, but a forwarded or shoulder-read link signs its holder in at aal1 without the emailed code D08 relies on. The owner also cannot tell this mail from a phishing attempt because the product never sends it on purpose.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `[auth.email.template.recovery]` with an Arabic body that carries no link or token («لا تُستخدم كلمات مرور في لوحة أنس؛ تجاهل هذه الرسالة»), set the same template on the hosted project (I28), and extend the hook to refuse `authentication_method = 'recovery'` as it refuses `password`.
findings.proof_recipe: curl -X POST $SUPABASE_URL/auth/v1/recover -H 'apikey: <publishable>' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"email":"<staff address>"}' → 200 and a 'Reset Password' mail in Inbucket/Mailpit whose body holds a /auth/v1/verify?token=…&type=recovery link; opening the link lands on site_url with #access_token=… (a live session). After the fix: the mail has no link and a recovery verify answers 403 from the hook.

findings.title: «تسجيل الخروج» ignores a failed signOut: with an expired access token and no network the stored refresh token survives while the screen shows the sign-in page
findings.evidence: AdminShell.tsx:128-134: `clearDrafts(); await getSupabaseBrowserClient().auth.signOut(); router.replace('/admin/sign-in')` — the result is never read. In @supabase/auth-js 2.117.1 (node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+auth-js@2.117.1/.../GoTrueClient.js:3430-3433) `_signOut` returns `{ error: sessionError }` before `removeCurrentSession()` when `_useSession` fails; `__loadSession` (lines 2544-2570) fails that way when the stored access token is past `expires_at` and the refresh request errors (offline), leaving the session object with its refresh token in localStorage.
findings.impact: On a shared or borrowed computer: the owner opens the admin after more than an hour away, the connection drops, he presses «تسجيل الخروج», sees the sign-in page and leaves. The next person who opens /admin once the network is back is signed in as him (the refresh token is still valid; Supabase refresh tokens 'never expire'). Narrow precondition (expired token + offline at the click), bounded impact (one device).
findings.proposed_fix: Read the result: `const { error } = await supabase.auth.signOut(); if (error) { setGate({status:'error'}) /* «تعذّر تسجيل الخروج؛ تحقق من الشبكة» */; return }` and only then redirect; keep `clearDrafts()` after the successful call.

findings.title: Rich-text links that pass the editor and the publish gate can vanish on the public page: the schema accepts `HTTPS://`, `https:host` and `https:/host`, the renderer requires the literal `https://`
findings.evidence: richtext.tsx:31 `node.url.startsWith('https://')`. src/admin/richtext.ts:25 `httpsUrl = z.url({ protocol: /^https$/ })`; Zod 4.6.5 (node_modules/zod/v4/core/schemas.js:232-236) applies its `://` guard only when the protocol regex equals its own `httpProtocol` source, so `URL.parse` normalises these. Verified with node: `HTTPS://a.com`, `https:a.com`, `https:/a.com` → schema success, `startsWith('https://')` false. RichTextEditor.tsx:95 and 215 use the same `httpsUrl`, so «تطبيق الرابط» accepts them and the paste transform keeps them.
findings.impact: An editor who types the address with caps lock on (or pastes `https:example.com`) gets no error, publishes, and the public page (and the admin preview, which uses the same renderer) shows the words as plain text with no link; nothing tells anyone. Not a security hole: the renderer still never emits a non-https href.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the two rules one: in richtext.tsx test `/^https:\/\//i.test(url)` and let the renderer normalise with `new URL(url).href`, or tighten `httpsUrl` with `.regex(/^https:\/\//)` so the editor refuses what the renderer drops. Add the three strings to tests/unit/richtext.test.ts.

findings.title: The baseline `_headers` sends no Strict-Transport-Security while the soon page on the same domain already does; the launch headers list omits HSTS and Permissions-Policy
findings.evidence: public/_headers:3-6 (`/*`) sends nosniff, Referrer-Policy and the four CSP directives only. artifacts/soon/site/_headers:10 sends `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` on anas.studio today. PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:101 (the headers paragraph) and PLANS/VERIFICATION.md:45 (P10) list CSP, nosniff and no-store, never HSTS or Permissions-Policy; grep of PLANS/ and docs/ for 'Strict-Transport|HSTS|Permissions-Policy' finds nothing outside the soon page. Cloudflare Pages adds no HSTS by default (https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/serving-pages/: default headers are Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Referrer-Policy, nosniff, Etag, Content-Type, Server).
findings.impact: When the product replaces the soon Worker on anas.studio, browsers that never saw the soon page get no HSTS unless the zone setting is turned on by hand; a first visit typed as http:// is one 301 away from a downgrade on a hostile network, and the staff sign-in page lives on this origin. Permissions-Policy is absent, so a future third-party script could use camera, geolocation or payment APIs unrestricted. Both are one line each and are not tracked anywhere in the plan.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to the `/*` block: `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` and `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()`; record in DATA-AND-SECURITY's headers paragraph and in I46/P10 that HSTS is sent by `_headers` (or by the zone, with the setting named) so P11 checks it on the hosted preview.

findings.title: A lost or reset authenticator locks the owner out of every step-up action: a verified TOTP factor can only be unenrolled at aal2, the admin offers no replacement, and no runbook covers it
findings.evidence: MfaEnroll.tsx:42-46: when a verified TOTP factor exists the screen renders only «تطبيق المصادقة مفعّل.» — no unenroll, no re-enrol. Supabase Auth (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supabase/auth/master/internal/api/mfa.go): `if factor.IsVerified() && !session.IsAAL2() { ... "AAL2 required to unenroll verified factor" }` and `if numVerifiedFactors > 0 && ... !session.IsAAL2() { "AAL2 required to enroll a new factor" }`, so without the old device no API call the browser can make removes or replaces the factor. docs/operations.md mentions TOTP only as a prerequisite (lines 562, 927-932, 1002, 1097); grep of docs/ and PLANS/ for 'unenroll|lost phone|new phone|mfa_factors' finds no recovery procedure (only the privacy-erase SQL deletes factors).
findings.impact: Anas changes or loses his phone without migrating the authenticator app: refunds, external-refund records, disputes, seller settings, policy approval, the checkout switch, invites, role changes and revokes all answer STEP_UP_REQUIRED and the dialog can never be satisfied. The only way back is a Supabase dashboard or SQL deletion of his row in auth.mfa_factors by whoever holds the project — on a Friday evening that may be nobody.
findings.proposed_fix: Write the recovery step into docs/operations.md and the owner training (P11): in the Supabase dashboard, Authentication → Users → the owner → remove the TOTP factor (or `delete from auth.mfa_factors where user_id = …` as postgres), then re-enrol in «الأمان»; tell Anas to keep the authenticator's backup/export. Optionally let a second active owner trigger the removal through staff-admin at aal2 (`admin.auth.admin.mfa.deleteFactor`), audited.

findings.title: The store build trusts `products.cover_image` as free text: a non-id value becomes an `` on the public store, unlike every content image, which the build re-validates
findings.evidence: store.ts:29 `cover_image: z.string().nullable()` with no shape rule; store.ts:126 `replaceMediaIds(row.cover_image, covers, MEDIA_ORIGIN)` and src/lib/images.ts:29-38 render any string that `parseMediaRef` accepts (`media|<base>|WxH|widths`) as `src="<base>/<w>.webp"` from any origin. The database allows it: 20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:120 `cover_image text check (... char_length between 1 and 120)`, and only the owner may write it (products_update_owner). Content images go through `imageIdSchema` (src/admin/fields.ts:266-268: a manifest key or `isMediaId`) in the build's `schema.parse`, so the same value in a room fails the build.
findings.impact: Only an owner session can write the column, so this is not exploitable by editors or visitors; but a `media|https://tracker.example/x|100x100|360` written through the Data API (a stolen owner session, a mis-typed import) ships a third-party image request on /store to every visitor, where the content path would have refused it at build time. Bounded, owner-only precondition.
findings.proposed_fix: In `productRowSchema`, validate `cover_image` with the same rule as content: `z.string().refine((id) => Object.hasOwn(imageManifest, id) || isMediaId(id)).nullable()` (or `.regex(uuid)` plus the manifest check), so the build fails like it does for rooms.

findings.title: check:export scans no `.mjs` file, so the pdf.js worker and any future module chunk in out/ are outside the secret and demo scan
findings.evidence: check-export.mjs:118 `const TEXT = /\.(html|txt|js|css|json|map|xml|webmanifest)$|[\\/]_headers$/`; `find out -name '*.mjs'` lists out/_next/static/media/pdf.worker.min.3bl-ygmetel-a.mjs (it even carries a fixture address, jm@kbswfq.pkbglt, which is how the gap showed). The demo guard also receives only `.html` and `.js` files (line 126).
findings.impact: No secret can land in a vendored worker today, so nothing is exposed; but the scan's promise 'no file contains a server-side secret' is narrower than stated, and a Next or pdf.js upgrade that emits `.mjs` chunks would be unscanned without any warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `mjs|cjs` to the TEXT pattern (and to the `built` filter), one word.

findings.title: A 5xx from Supabase Auth (SMTP or quota failure) is shown as «أرسلنا إليه رمزًا»: the masking meant for existence-revealing 4xx also hides a mail outage
findings.evidence: SignIn.tsx:43-52: `if (sendError && !sendError.status) → OFFLINE_MESSAGE; if (sendError?.status === 429) → RATE_LIMITED_MESSAGE; setMessage(SENT_MESSAGE); setStep('code')`. Any other status, including Supabase Auth's 500 `unexpected_failure` 'Error sending magic link email' when the custom SMTP (Resend) refuses the send, reaches the success branch. AUDIT-2 ADMIN-auth-8 fixed only the no-status (network) case.
findings.impact: During a Resend quota exhaustion (see CLIENT-SEC-01) or any SMTP outage, every staff member is told a code was sent and is moved to the code step; they wait out the ten minutes, retry, and get the same false sentence. Nobody learns that mail is down, so the owner home's mail warning is the only clue and only once someone is signed in.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat `sendError.status >= 500` like the network case with its own sentence («تعذّر إرسال الرمز الآن؛ حاول بعد قليل.») and stay on the email step; keep the masked success only for 2xx and 4xx.

doc_claims_checked.claim: Cloudflare Pages applies every matching _headers rule to a request and joins a header defined twice with a comma
doc_claims_checked.evidence: https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/headers/: 'An incoming request which matches multiple rules' URL patterns will inherit all rules' headers' and 'If a header is applied twice in the _headers file, the values are joined with a comma separator.' So /admin gets two CSP policies (both enforced) and /orders gets 'strict-origin-when-cross-origin, no-referrer' where the last valid token wins; this depends on the /* block staying first in the file.
